newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Traffic authorities are bracing themselves for a deluge of motorists returning from their Easter weekend holidays on Monday as the country's road death toll topped 200.
- Zaire's rebels say they are grabbing more territory in the mineral-rich Shaba region of the south, ahead of peace talks that could begin this week in South Africa.
- South African singer Miriam Makeba was the victim of abusive can-throwing hooligans at a rock concert held in the Karoo, in the Western Cape province.
- Three million supporters of the Zion Christian Church gathered at Moria City in the north of the country for their annual Easter pilgrimage.
- Shootouts between robbers and police left three people - a civilian and two robbers - dead on Sunday.

- President Nelson Mandela left for Mozambique on Sunday almost immediately after his arrival back in South Africa after a visit to India and Bangladesh. His spokesman said Mandela would spend a week relaxing in the company of his companion Graca Machel.
- South Africa is on the brink of closing a weapons deal with Britain, including British Aerospeace's Hawke fighter plane, worth more than 14 million rand.
